text: New Years day today and time to fulfill a yearly ritual to go out and eat some seafood,so based on positive Yelp reviews decided to visit Skidders. All in all it was a good experience and a great way to start off the New Year.Everything went smoothly and nothing major to report in the negative department so I'm giving them 5 stars,It was our first visit and we plan on returning to try some of their yummy looking Italian and Greek dishes.

Sides do not count so I got the king oyster mushroom and a couple others. They bring out 4 banchan. Fewest I have ever seen in similar K-bbq ayce. Usually, 10 or so at Gen Korean and OZ. Over the course of 2 hrs we got the spicy tofu soup, potstickers, gyoza and fried oysters, lemongrass chix and one more chix, a couple pork bellies and Hawaiian steak, most of the beef including bulgogis and calamari, spicy shrimp and baby octopus. We left most of the chicken alone, same with a few pork that were not bellies and did not go for the small beef intestines. Service was pretty good. It in no way competes with Gen Korean in Las Vegas. The waitstaff there teams up. I never had better service in ANY restaurant than at that Gen K (check out my review of them). However, the person grabbing empty places was on point. She would be there asap to grab empties and fill waters. The waitress would be back often enough but not that much once 4-5 tables were seated. But I did not starve waiting like some reviews saying the wait for the next round was long. She came around the right time when I was nearly done with a round so that new order would come when we finished the previous round. That is what counts! She also changed the grill 2x. Just oftem enough when they had char marks stuck on most areas. Green tea ice cream included topped off our experience. To conclude, a good joint for such fare in Sparks. I read reviews prior to coming and they have 1 other competitor in R/S. The other is Ijii4 which has a $19.99 lunch $29.99 dinner tag but a bunch more items and a 10% off Yelp for 1. Ijii is a 4.5 on Yelp and Siu comes in with a 4. I want to try Ijii next time Iam near Reno before deciding who wins the battle of the two warriors of KBBQ ayce game in this part of town. One + is that this place had overhead ventilation meaning our clothes did not smell like smoke afterwards like other ones I mentioned previously. Negative would be the menu for lunch is much smaller than Gen or OZ. Maybe 18 total items with chix, pork, beef and seafood not counting apps or soup. Gen and OZ maybe 30+. Absolute biggest negative was that they only include 4 banchan vs. 10+ elsewhere. Overlooking those 2 negatives would land them at a solid "4" rating in my book.

text: The Indiana Medical History Museum is located on the Central State Hospital Campus on West Vermont. This place is so cool if your a history buff, in the medical field or curious about the history of mental disease. So many stories and so much history to explore on the tour. Easy to find and parking isn't an issue. Note they are closed Sunday - Tuesday with open hours of 10a-4p, Wednesday through Saturday. The tour guides are very knowledgeable and friendly. The tours are approximately an hour and start on the hour. Doors are locked during a tour due to limited staff so arrive a few minutes before your tour. The last tour begins at 3:00 p.m. No reservations needed unless you are a group of 6 or more then call ahead preferably 3 weeks. The admission is only $10 for adults, $9 for seniors, $5 for college students with valid ID and only $3 for students under 18. Very affordable for families and groups plus an amazing amount of history surrounds you while hearing revealing, true stories. It definitely is a museum worth revisiting because it is difficult to catch and retain everything the first time through. The heart of the museum is the Old Pathology Building, the oldest surviving pathology facility in the nation. The Building is on the National Register of Historic Places. Inaugurated in 1896, the Pathological Department facilitated medical education and research on the physical causes of mental disease. In operation until the 1960s, the Pathological Department was reborn as a museum in 1969 and its scientifically equipped interior was left intact with several new pieces donated over the years. You'll view the Teaching Amphitheater, the Autopsy room where organ were retained to study, the Anatomical Museum and lab room, the Morgue, the Photography Room, the Clinical Laboratory and the Histology Lab to name a few. The doctors were diligently working to discover the causes of depression, dementia and schizophrenia. I was amazed at the number of interesting stories we heard and truly saw how much has changed in a 100 years. A very enjoyable and instructive tour plus they try to answer all questions if possible. I highly recommend if you're searching for something different to do for an hour even if you have no medical background. Are you an avid history buff? The tour is afforable, enjoyable and you'll appreciate how far our medical history has come in a 100 years. Note, not suitable for small children, those with issues of discussions concerning death, autopsies, or viewing body parts and skeletons. Some squeamish folks could have issues.

I thought the meal had a nicely balanced flavor and the thick noodles were lightly coated. The veggies could have been cut a little smaller, but otherwise, they were fine. Each entree came with a cup of soup (fuller flavor than most places I've been), a small gingered salad, and a crisp spring roll with a sweet dipping sauce. text: The Hank's Manifesto By Dr M Herzberg A neighborhood can be compared to a living organism. Its streets are the veins, its homes are the skin, its trees and plants are the lungs, and its many varied inhabitants are the brain and central nervous system. But as any scientist (such as myself) can tell you, no organism can survive without a heart. In the case of the organism that is the Marigny/Bywater, Hank's fulfills that role. This is true on a physical level: Hank's moves our bloodstream by providing it with precious resources such as 40's of malt beverages, corn dogs, "tobacco" pipes, Roquefort cheese, canned beans, etcetera. But more importantly, Hank's is the neighborhood's spiritual heart. People come to Hank's from all walks of life to heal, to escape the nihilist horror and alienation which day-to-day life in our capitalist society inevitably accompany. Hank's cares not whether you have won today's battle with your inner daemons or whether guilt and shame consumes you. Hank's is here for you to listen, without judgement, and to bless your broken soul. Yes, they were allegedly anti-semites, back in days of yore. That's a big no-no. But this era of hatred has passed, as the employees who perpetrated these vile injustices have been tried and punished in the international court of Hank's. The banality of evil has been replaced with the totality of love and understanding. The new Hankers are people of honor and integrity, and they will hold your head on their bosoms and sing their sweet lullabies as you weep your tears of sorrow, washing away years of emotional repression and resentment. The pressing question remains: who is Hank? Is Hank the owner who benevolently smiles at us from his hidden palace? Is Hank the lady who makes the fried chicken in disguise? Is Hank the crusty in the parking lot who asks you for 47 cents? Hank remains a misunderstood figure, because in truth, there is no one Hank. Hank is an ethereal concept: we are all Hank. As such I invite you to see for yourself the greatest organization in this country, nay, on this planet. Be it for an afternoon shrimp po-boy (with extra hot sauce) or a handjob in the parking lot (not officially endorsed by Hank's, but they'll provide you with lube and napkins), come and awaken your inner ubermensch as you do away with the corpse of Judeo-Christian morality and see the truth beyond good and evil: Hank.

text: You can often tell if an authentic Chinese restaurant is worth its salt by a few markers. Does it offer a character-appropriate, bilingual menu? Check. Does it have tried and true boba tea offerings, even fare like honey lemon tea? Check. Does it have at least one English misspelling on the menu displayed at the front but a clever Chinese idiom name? Double check. You know you're in a great, not good, place when the staff has thoughtfully placed electric buttons for service in the corner, disposable napkins dispensed like tissues on the table, and encased the tablecloths in glass. Now, what to order? Honestly, anything off of the noodle menu. It is, after all, a noodle house. The Chongqing Noodles are the restaurant's namesake, so I suggest either the house favorite or Zhou's beef noodle soup. I admit, the quality of the noodles themselves are a bit wanting. I highly recommend handpulled noodles, but you are yet to unlockthat particular level in the Nashville area. Given that competition is relatively low in Nashville for proper Chinese fare, this is by far one of the best noodle shops given its outstanding (albeit still relatively high) price point. When a restaurant has cheese milk foam drinks on its menu in the South, you have to hope for nothing but its success. Nashville's international student population needs this. Honestly, Nashville locals need this injection of culture. I'm not saying this is the next Din Tai Fung or Kung Fu Tea. However, at a local level with low competition? Meet Noodles blows everything else out of the water. Just make sure to order in Chinese or order with someone who can to get the full, proper cuisine experience.

I ended up sitting outside my building in the middle of the night until 4am. I called and emailed management the next day, no response of course. There's also no A/C once again and it's been unbearably hot in the building for days. What is Alden Park doing for its residents during these constant outages? There's been no air conditioning for more than half the summer. Is there going to be a rent deduction? People have animals and young children on high floors and it's unlivable. I remember before moving in I saw all the horrible reviews and thought "well, in any large complex there are going to be some complainers," so I chose to ignore them and move in anyway. I've never regretted anything more, I can't wait to get out of here. The few positive reviews of Alden Park are left by office staff or their significant others/friends. How unethical is that? When I moved in, management told me to expect rent increases of two to three percent. At renewal, they raised my rent nearly ten percent (!) and tacked on new fees like a $25/month amenity fee even though our amenities are open to the public. We also pay fees for trash removal, but there's no recycling and trash isn't even removed for days, so the trash rooms collect vermin and odors. ------------------------------

I guess our salesman saw a better opportunity across the store? Not clear, since there was still no explanation given. New salesperson/clerk asked us for a deposit without being able to provide the cost for each rental. We were told that he wouldn't know the exact pricing until everything was put into the system, but it couldn't be put into the system without a deposit. (um, what? I'm not giving you my money when I don't even have a price or rental agreement). I asked him to enter the choices and our info into the system so that we could get pricing,. He did so, and STILL could not provide us with the definitive cost to each of our groomsman. The price was "gonna be arounnnd $150-160, give or take with tax you know," When I said we'd like to shop around, and asked if he could keep our info on file, we were told that he could keep the paper copy for us, but someone would have to re-enter everything into the computer again. This is when another employee walked by and VERY rudely, overly loudly, and with much attitude said that "this is why it doesn't go in the system without a deposit because now there's no way to remove it." That's when we thanked them for our time and walked out. There was no need to speak to anyone that way, whether it was to another employee or (clearly the case) directed toward us. Sorry MW, but if you're going to provide a service in the wedding industry you need to step it up in a lot of ways. I wouldn't go back there if even the rentals were free. We did not feel like a priority, we didn't get a sense of confidence from the employees, and quite honestly, the options we were presented were quite limited with no suggestions outside the box for alternatives. text: This was the first time I've ever had a restaurant tell me "Our kitchen is too busy for your order, we cannot take your order at this time". Unbelievable - you have a customer who wants a single pizza and you won't let her order? I had spent a good part of the afternoon searching for a Roman style Salami pizza. It's my favorite, my go-to spots are Alice and Rione in Center City which I went to. Alice on 15th was not selling it today, Alice on Market and Rione were both closed. I was ready to go to Giant and make my own Salami pizza but this restaurant called Royal Cafe in Narberth had been on my list for some time and they did have Salami pizza! It was 5:30 PM on a Saturday so I called ahead to see how things were going. A young girl answered the phone and every question I asked was met with a shaky "Umm" answer. Simple questions like, "What time is your happy hour?, Do you have happy hour on the weekends? What is your wait time for a party of two right now?" She proceeded to tell me they weren't taking anymore walk-in parties for the night (I can respect that) but they also weren't allowed to take to-go orders because the kitchen was too busy. In all the restaurants I've ever been to in my life, I have literally never heard that. If your kitchen is backed up, tell me "orders are taking longer than usual" which is fine - I'll wait for it! But to assume the customer is unwilling to wait for the order and not allowing them to even place an order felt so insulting and disappointing. You have people wanting to try your food and you're turning them down? What kind of hospitality is that. So anyway, due to the uneasy answers we were getting on the phone, we decide to go in person anyway. We pull into the parking lot, immediately get a spot and see 3 open picnic tables (so busy my butt). I get to the front and they say "3 hour wait for a party of 2 (they said they weren't seating anymore walk-ins on the phone, so which is it?) and I ask again, "Can I place a take-out order?" She says the kitchen has instructed her not to accept any other orders and I tell her I want 1 single pizza. She agrees to double check and what do you know, they're able to do it. 10 minutes later, the pizza is done and as I'm paying for it (which by the way, the front desk lady doesn't know how to login to the tablet so a different lady takes my card and runs away with it inside to use a different kiosk without telling me), I hear another front desk lady on the phone explaining the menu to another patron who is clearly placing a take-out order (literally reading ingredients out to patrons over the phone and placing this massive 4-6 person meal order). I can't believe I got so much pushback for wanting to place a single pizza order but they can accommodate such a large take-out order. My husband and I just moved to Wynnewood and were really excited to try this place, but after that experience, I'm not quite jumping at the opportunity again. Not until they 1) Fix their customer service, 2) Work on their communication between the kitchen and the front desk. Things to note: 1) make a reservation on a Saturday or don't expect to be seated. 2) Happy hour is 4-5:30 (earlier than most places) Tuesday through Sunday. 3) Parking can be tough, the lot is pretty small and just adjacent to the eating area so good luck. As for the food, we got the Murder Hornet for $16. Crust was fluffy, medium-sized pizza came out hot, lots of salami on there and totally smothered in honey - the only redeeming factor of this review. I know this restaurant is only 6 weeks old but if you're not ready to handle customers, then scale things back rather than customers having a rough experience.

He then informed me that people actually start calling at 11am for orders...and their pizzas are so "special" it takes awhile to make with the oven blah blah blah. By the way, this guy lacks any sense of urgency or empathy. If you start taking orders at 11, then start telling your eager customers so they can plan accordingly!! Why was this the first I'm hearing of this?? Being from the east coast, I am just accustomed to better customer service. Places get busy all the time. It's about the way you handle it. Instead of saying "sure" and telling me about your stupid "gigantic" wait, you should say...."wow thanks so much for supporting a new business, we have actually been doing so well people are calling in really early to place their orders. I'd be happy to put it in for you now, but it'll be 2 hours but I promise it'll be worth the wait! If not, call tomorrow early and I promise we will get that cooking for you". text: We stopped in after making reservations for an early Saturday evening dinner. Overall, we had good food, generous portions, and a pleasant server. However, there were a few things about the place that could use some attention. After parking in the Circle Centre Mall, we strolled down Meridian and entered. The interior of the restaurant is broken into lots of small rooms and a bar that you can partially see from the entry. There is also a Host lectern that was unmanned, so we waited a couple minutes for anyone of the staff to greet us. I don't understand the point of having a station for a host and not having anyone there. But since we had reservations, someone eventually arrived and seated us to the right in one of the small rooms. We waited a few minutes and our waitress arrived and took our beverage orders. We watched as two other couples arrived and left because no one was there to greet them. Some other people arrived and seated themselves at the bar. It was becoming a pattern of confusion about seating. After our beverages arrive, we quickly placed our orders to make sure the food was put in the queue. Although we never had that long to wait, we rarely saw any staff during the visit because of our secluded room. It felt odd. By mid-meal, we noticed that one of the male servers was telling guests that there was a 30 minute wait. We had a 6-person table in our nook that was unfilled and I could see a 4-person table unused across the way. Did they simply not have enough staff to man the tables? Again, it seemed like a lost revenue opportunity for the restaurant because ALL the customers who were told of the delay left. Fortunately, our food arrived in a timely fashion and it was quite good. I had a starter cup of Guinness Onion Soup that had a delightful flavor. There wasn't any actual broth since their version has garlic bread cubes in the soup that absorbed all the broth. The onions were so cooked that they were there in flavor, but not visible (they must have completely broken down into the broth.) The cheese topping was melted and easy to dig through with a spoon which made eating the soup very easy. Really good flavor. The only real negative was that the house bread was a bit dry and without any broth to dip it in, it was less than I had hoped. I also ordered the fish 'n chips. A large single piece of battered white fish came with lots of seasoned potato wedges, cole slaw, and tartar sauce. Good flavor without being overcooked made for a filling meal. Note that they do have malt vinegar on the tables for those who prefer it to tartar sauce. My wife got the Paddy Mac Sandwich with the corned beef replaced by smoked turkey. It comes with cole slaw on the sandwich along with Swiss cheese, 1000 Island dressing and served on marbled rye and a side of the potato wedges. She thought the flavor was pretty good but though the ratio of turkey to cole slaw was light on the turkey. As I mentioned above, we enjoyed our meal and found our server to be pleasant though some small delays occurred. I hope they can use this review to address the lack of a greeting to customers who are coming in out of the cold and have nobody to talk to. Review #3332
